summary: Across 10.2 reconstructed minutes, 7 experiments finished; 4 were compute-bound. The 10.03-minute Three-family exact intervention response surface determined elapsed completion time. Phase attribution is unavailable, while the locked compute-bound idle indicator is false.
bottlenecks_identified: Almost all reconstructed elapsed time is assigned to the 10.03-minute Three-family exact intervention response surface, but the data gives no internal timing to locate the cost.
The idle GPU monitor snapshot has no link to compute-task intervals, so the data cannot rate accelerator efficiency beyond the locked false idle indicator.
The records omit simultaneous model count and runner choice, which prevents an audit of DualGPURunner eligibility and dispatch.
improvements_suggested: Add task-owned timers for setup, model loading, inference, output writing, and cleanup.
Capture task-linked GPU utilization and memory receipts throughout each compute-bound execution window.
Record simultaneous model count and runner selection at launch, and select DualGPURunner only when 2 or more models run in parallel.
Add a fail-fast accelerator-engagement check that applies only to compute-bound tasks.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Instrument the response-surface workflow with phase timers to locate its critical-path cost.
Attach GPU samples to task start and stop receipts so compute utilization can be audited.
Add launch receipts for model concurrency and conditional DualGPURunner selection.
meta_reflection: Fallback timing isolates the duration leader but cannot locate the work inside it. Task-linked phase, accelerator, and model-concurrency receipts must precede any savings estimate or parallel-runner diagnosis.
